title: The Gilded Spire Again
premise: Dominic Whitlock has spent fifteen years as the quiet keeper of the Gilded Spire, a sealed gate between the human city of Vell and the fading realm of Auren, selling harmless charms while pretending the wards need no tending. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Dominic learns the covenant binding the realms was broken by their own mother, a former gatekeeper who traded the other side's warmth for Vell's safety. Pursued by the city's wardens and guided by Sable, an exiled Auren emissary they once loved and betrayed, Dominic must journey into the dying other realm to reforge the covenant with their own blood. In the end, Dominic chooses love over duty by becoming the living seal themselves, holding the gate open just enough for starlight to return, at the cost of their memories of everyone they saved.
about_author: Odile Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters between estranged siblings before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in early, and claims her best ideas arrive with it.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On an ordinary market day, Dominic sells a luck charm to a nervous warden's daughter, then watches the sky go black and feels the Spire's wards shatter through their bones. Among the panicked crowds they glimpse Sable, alive after fifteen years. The emotional beat is dread laced with longing: the past Dominic buried has come knocking.

chapters.title: What Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic and Sable POV. Hiding in the undercity, Sable reveals that Dominic's mother broke the covenant deliberately, hoarding Auren's warmth to save Vell from a plague, dooming the other realm to winter. Wardens close in, forcing a choice. The beat is bitter revelation: inheritance is not a gift but a debt, and Dominic owes both worlds.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falling
chapters.summary: Sable POV, with Dominic present. Crossing into Auren, they find a beautiful realm freezing star by star, its people forgetting their own names. At the ruined covenant-stone, the ritual demands a life freely given; Sable offers theirs before Dominic can speak. The climax burns with sacrifice and confession: love declared aloud in a place built on silence.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Open Gate
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Refusing Sable's death, Dominic pours their own memories into the stone instead, becoming the living seal that lets starlight leak back into both realms. They wake in Vell, beloved by people they no longer remember, as the first stars return. The resolution lands on tender ambiguity: some inheritances must be paid forward, not kept.
